**Commercial VRP expands beyond subscriptions toward everyday payments**

*Industry leaders at Open Banking Expo flagged bill payments, e-commerce and account top-ups as the next growth areas for commercial VRP, with adoption now tied to the UK Payments Initiative's ability to bring banks beyond the original mandated providers on board.*

Payments specialists speaking at Open Banking Expo UK and Europe 2026 outlined how commercial variable recurring payments (VRP) are entering a new adoption phase, with use cases extending into utility bill payments, retail e-commerce and investment account top-ups. Panellists pointed to recent live deployments, including InvestEngine's reported 98% success rate and Modulr's launch under the UK Payments Initiative, as evidence that the infrastructure is now mature enough for broader merchant adoption.

The discussion highlighted that instant settlement and lower transaction costs give commercial VRP a structural advantage over card-on-file for recurring but variable-amount payments. However, speakers acknowledged that consumer awareness remains low and that merchant integration requires effort to match the frictionless experience card networks offer.

The conversation also touched on the role of the UK's new domestic payments scheme in driving adoption. With GoCardless and Moneyhub already participating in the UK Payments Initiative, commercial VRP has a distribution channel that did not exist six months ago. Whether banks beyond the original mandated providers will support commercial VRP voluntarily remains the open question for the product's trajectory.

*Sources: [Commercial VRP approaches wider adoption as industry highlights new payment opportunities](https://www.openbankingexpo.com/news/commercial-vrp-approaches-wider-adoption-as-industry-highlights-new-payment-opportunities/) — Openbankingexpo*

**Deutsche Bank and Ant map agentic AI roadmap for wholesale banking**

*A joint research report identifies institutional treasury, cross-border payments and trade finance as the domains where autonomous AI agents could first reshape wholesale banking operations.*

Deutsche Bank and Ant Digital Technologies have published a joint research report setting out how agentic AI could be integrated into wholesale banking. The report identifies three priority domains: institutional treasury management, cross-border payments and trade finance, each characterised by high volumes of structured data and repetitive decision-making that lend themselves to autonomous processing.

European banks are moving from pilots to production deployments of agentic payments. Credit Agricole completed France's first production agentic payment in June, and ING, Worldline and Mastercard ran Europe's first agentic transaction the same month. Deutsche Bank's report focuses on the wholesale side, where operational complexity and value per transaction are both higher.

The report frames agentic AI less as a consumer-facing novelty and more as a back-office transformation tool. The wholesale emphasis suggests that the near-term commercial case for agentic AI in banking may lie in cost reduction and speed improvements on existing workflows rather than in new product categories.

*Sources: [Deutsche Bank and Ant set out roadmap for integrating agentic AI into wholesale banking](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48740/deutsche-bank-and-ant-set-out-roadmap-for-integrating-agentic-ai-into-wholesale-banking?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**Revolut adds Uber to its growing European account-to-account payments network**

*The integration across more than 25 markets follows similar deals with Just Eat, Glovo, Booking.com and Amazon, turning Revolut Pay into a proprietary challenger to card networks at checkout.*

Revolut is integrating Revolut Pay as a native checkout option on Uber and Uber Eats across the UK and Europe, giving more than five million shared customers an account-to-account alternative to card payments. Customers authorise each transaction via biometric authentication in the Revolut app, bypassing card details entirely. Revolut claims an average authorisation rate of 98.5% and is using a promotional RevPoints multiplier, running from November 11 to January 6, 2027, to drive adoption.

The deal is one of a series that together amount to a distribution strategy: Revolut Pay is now embedded in the checkout flows of Just Eat, Glovo, Booking.com and Amazon across European markets. For Uber, the appeal is lower payment costs and fewer failed transactions. For Revolut, each integration extends its acquiring footprint into high-frequency consumer spending categories without needing the kind of broad merchant acceptance that open banking-based pay-by-bank services have struggled to achieve.

The approach diverges from the open banking model. Rather than relying on standardised APIs and bank-initiated payment flows, Revolut Pay operates as a closed-loop system routed through its own app and accounts. The commercial question is whether rewards-driven adoption persists once promotional incentives taper, and whether the model scales beyond Revolut's existing customer base.

*Sources: [Uber adds Revolut Pay in big boost for A2A payments](https://paymentexpert.com/2026/11/11/uber-revolut-pay-boost-a2a-payments/) — Payment Expert*

**Bank of Finland ties digital euro to European economic security**

*A speech by the Bank of Finland frames payment infrastructure independence, including the digital euro and instant payments, as essential to Europe's strategic resilience.*

Olli Rehn, governor of the Bank of Finland, is framing European payment infrastructure autonomy as a core element of economic security. Speaking on strategic resilience in Finland and Europe, Rehn argued that the digital euro and the instant payments regulation together represent the means by which Europe can reduce its dependence on non-European payment networks.

The speech echoes themes raised by the Bank of Finland in May 2026, when the central bank framed European payment autonomy as a geopolitical imperative, and by the French Banking Federation in July. Rehn's intervention adds weight at a moment when the European Parliament has advanced the digital euro legislation to final negotiations and when the ECB has selected network service providers for the platform. The consistent framing from Nordic, Southern European and now Finnish central bankers suggests a durable political consensus behind the sovereignty argument.

Rehn cautioned that economic security should not become a pretext for protectionism, a nuance that distinguishes his position from more hawkish interventions elsewhere. The speech positions instant payments infrastructure and the digital euro as complements rather than competitors to private-sector innovation, a framing that aligns with the ECB's own messaging under Piero Cipollone, the executive board member responsible for the digital euro.

*Sources: [Economic Security and Strategic Resilience in Finland and in Europe](https://www.suomenpankki.fi/en/news-and-topical/speeches-and-interviews2/2026/economic-security-and-strategic-resilience-in-finland-and-in-europe/) — Suomen Pankki*
